summary:
Moon Racing is an interactive space exploration game designed to help young students experience the challenges of being an astronaut and planetary scientist.

In this project, we developed a 2D simulation where players control a six-wheeled rover to explore the Moon and Mars. The game features realistic physics, challenging terrain, obstacles, fuel management, a Nitro system, and interactive scientific missions. Players complete research activities such as collecting rock samples, studying craters, searching for water ice, measuring temperatures, and growing potatoes in a simulated space greenhouse. The environments are inspired by NASA's planetary research and terrain data.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming complex space science concepts into fun, hands-on learning experiences. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, students can experiment, solve problems, and make decisions like real astronauts.

Moon Racing is important because it encourages curiosity, critical thinking, creativity, and interest in STEM education, inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Project Name: Moon Racing – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Project Type: Interactive Educational Space Exploration Game

Project Overview

Moon Racing is a 2D educational space exploration game developed by our team to help young students experience the challenges of being astronauts and planetary scientists.

Our goal is to make space science more accessible, interactive, and enjoyable by combining scientific knowledge with engaging gameplay.

What We Developed

We created a browser-based game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Players control a six-wheeled rover to explore two environments: the Moon and Mars.

The game includes:

  • Planetary Exploration: Explore simulated lunar and Martian landscapes inspired by NASA's research and terrain data.
  • Realistic Driving Mechanics: Experience different gravitational conditions, uneven terrain, obstacles, fuel management, and vehicle physics.
  • 20 Scientific Missions: Complete 10 research challenges on each planet, including collecting rock samples, measuring craters, searching for water ice, identifying minerals, and constructing a research base.
  • Space Agriculture: Grow potatoes in a virtual greenhouse by preparing soil, watering plants, monitoring growth, and harvesting crops.
  • Interactive Learning: Answer astronomy questions and learn about planetary environments before beginning each expedition.
  • Bilingual Support: Play in English or Vietnamese.

How Our Project Solves the Challenge

The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge encourages students to understand the skills and knowledge required for space exploration.

Moon Racing addresses this challenge by allowing players to practice scientific observation, problem-solving, resource management, and decision-making through interactive missions.

Instead of only studying astronomy through textbooks, students can apply scientific concepts in a simulated environment.

Why Our Project Matters

Space exploration requires curiosity, creativity, teamwork, and scientific thinking.

Our project encourages young learners to develop these skills while discovering the challenges of exploring other worlds.

By making STEM education engaging and accessible, we hope Moon Racing will inspire more students to become future scientists, engineers, and astronauts.

Technology and Accessibility

Moon Racing runs directly in a web browser without requiring additional software installation. Its planetary environments are educational simulations informed by NASA resources rather than direct reconstructions of real exploration routes.
